raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old renal transplant recipient presented with fever of 2-month duration in August 2008. Five years back, he had undergone renal transplantation with his sister as donor. His basic kidney disease was unknown and he was on triple immunosuppression with cyclosporine (CsA), azathioprine (AZA) and prednisolone. His baseline serum creatinine was 1.2 mg/dl. In addition to the fever, he also complained of malaise and weight loss of 5 kg during the last 2 months. He had no history of cough, expectoration, loose stools, dysuria or increased urinary frequency. He had no history of tuberculosis in the past.
On examination, he was febrile and had pallor but there were no palpable lymph nodes. His blood pressure was 130/90 mmHg. Examination of the various organ systems was essentially unremarkable.
His hemoglobin was 9.2 g/dl, total leukocyte count 2400/mm3, platelet count of 160 x 103/ mm3, erythrocyte sedimentation rate 30 mm/1st hour, serum creatinine was 1 mg/dl, sodium 142 mEq/L, potassium 4.7 mEq/L, serum bilirubin 0.73 mg/dl, aspartate aminotransferase 40 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase 26 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 446 IU/L, serum total protein 7.5 g/dl, serum albumin 3.4 g/dl and the fasting serum glucose was 104 mg/dl. Ultrasonography of the abdomen revealed 5 x 6 cm hypo-echoic lesion in segment V of the liver. A contrast- enhanced computed tomographic scan of the thorax and abdomen revealed multiple, confluent hypodense lesions in the liver, spleen, the renal allograft [Figure 1] and prostate [Figure 2], along with multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the mesentery with central necrosis. The prostate showed multiple air specks also. The high-resolution computed tomography of lungs showed typical miliary pattern. Fine-needle aspiration cytology from the lesion in the liver showed numerous acid-fast bacilli; acid- fast bacilli were also demonstrated in the overnight urine sample. A bone marrow examination, which was performed in view of persistent leucopenia, showed hypocellularity with megaloblastosis, but there were no acid-fast bacilli or granuloma seen. HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen) and anti-HCV (hepatitis C virus) antibody were negative, HIV serology was non-reactive and his serum was negative for Cytomegalovirus DNA. Urine cultures performed repeatedly were sterile despite persistent pyuria.
He was started on 4-drug anti-tuberculous therapy (ATT) with isoniazid, ciprofloxacin, ethmbutol and pyrazinamide. AZA was stopped in view of the severe leucopenia. The cyclosporine dose was also reduced. He became afebrile by the end of first week of ATT. He also required treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor as the leucopenia worsened further despite discontinuation of AZA.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old male renal transplant recipient presenting with persistent fever, malaise, and weight loss for two months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 2-month history of continuous daily fever, malaise, and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg. He denied cough, sputum production, diarrhea, dysuria, or urinary frequency.
subjective.past_medical_history: Living-donor renal transplant recipient (allograft from sister 5 years prior; baseline serum creatinine 1.2 mg/dL) maintained on triple immunosuppressive therapy comprising cyclosporine (CsA), azathioprine (AZA), and prednisolone. Unknown primary kidney disease. No previous personal history of tuberculosis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Persistent fever, generalized malaise, 5 kg weight loss. Denies cough, expectoration, gastrointestinal disturbance, or urinary symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile, pale, blood pressure 130/90 mmHg. No peripheral lymphadenopathy. Systemic examination of cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurological systems was unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, total leukocyte count 2,400/mm3, platelet count 160 x 10^3/mm3, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 30 mm/1st hr. Serum creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, sodium 142 mEq/L, potassium 4.7 mEq/L, total bilirubin 0.73 mg/dL, AST 40 IU/L, ALT 26 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 446 IU/L, total protein 7.5 g/dL, serum albumin 3.4 g/dL, fasting serum glucose 104 mg/dL. Urinalysis showed persistent pyuria; repeated routine urine cultures were sterile. Serologies for HBsAg, anti-HCV, and HIV were negative; serum Cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA was negative. Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a 5 x 6 cm hypoechoic lesion in segment V of the liver.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced CT of thorax and abdomen revealed multiple confluent hypodense lesions in the liver, spleen, renal allograft, and prostate (with multiple air specks), along with multiple centrally necrotic mesenteric lymph nodes. High-resolution CT (HRCT) of the lungs showed a typical diffuse miliary pattern. Bone marrow biopsy (performed for persistent leukopenia) revealed hypocellularity with megaloblastosis, without acid-fast bacilli or granulomas.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated miliary tuberculosis involving the lungs, liver, spleen, renal allograft, prostate, mesenteric lymph nodes, and urinary tract in an immunosuppressed renal allograft recipient.
Diagnostic confirmation: Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the liver lesion demonstrated numerous acid-fast bacilli; acid-fast bacilli were also demonstrated in an overnight concentrated urine specimen.
Management and outcome: Initiated on 4-drug anti-tuberculosis therapy (ATT) consisting of isoniazid, ciprofloxacin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide. Azathioprine was discontinued and cyclosporine dosage was reduced due to worsening leukopenia; granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) was administered. Patient defervesced by the end of the first week of ATT, with favorable clinical stabilization.
